algorithm.Title: Sweating - Female (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Female
Definition: Excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis) assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published excessive sweating guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for sweating with chest pain, abnormal breathing, fainting, confusion, seizure, stroke signs, severe weakness, suspected hypoglycaemia, heat illness, poisoning/carbon monoxide, sepsis, or pregnancy/postpartum danger signs. Move from heat or a suspected exposure only if safe and do not give food, drink, or medicine if consciousness/swallowing is impaired. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Did the sweating begin during or after possible exposure to a faulty heater, generator, fire, charcoal, gas appliance, or enclosed-space fumes?
questions.Information: Symptoms associated with possible carbon monoxide exposure belong in the Carbon Monoxide Exposure pathway.

questions.Question: Along with the sweating, is there chest pain, difficulty breathing, confusion, or fainting?
questions.Information: Sudden profuse sweating combined with chest pain, breathing difficulty, confusion, or fainting is a recognized red flag for a serious underlying cause (such as a heart attack or severe infection) and needs immediate emergency care.

questions.Question: Has the sweating lasted at least 6 months, does it happen at least weekly or interfere with daily activities, does it happen at night, is there a family history, or is it not helped by things tried so far?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends clinical review for these persistent, functionally-limiting, or unexplained sweating patterns.

questions.Question: Is this mild, occasional sweating with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes mild sweating as manageable at home with clothing and antiperspirant measures.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency sweating-associated response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for sweating with chest pain, abnormal breathing, fainting, confusion, seizure, stroke signs, severe weakness, suspected hypoglycaemia, heat illness, poisoning/carbon monoxide, sepsis, or pregnancy/postpartum danger signs. Move from heat or a suspected exposure only if safe and do not give food, drink, or medicine if consciousness/swallowing is impaired. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening chest pain or breathing; confusion, fainting, seizure, or weakness; heat, poisoning, infection, or glucose emergency.

advice.Title: Urgent sweating review
Content: Arrange a primary-care appointment to investigate the cause and discuss treatment options.
Call Back If: new symptoms develop; sweating worsens.

advice.Title: Governed care for non-urgent sweating
Content: Use loose breathable clothing, change damp clothing/socks, maintain usual fluids if not restricted, and avoid known triggers. Antiperspirant or medicine advice requires age, pregnancy/breastfeeding, skin integrity, endocrine/cardiac conditions, interactions, and approved Qatar pharmacy guidance. New night sweats, weight loss, fever, medicine/substance change, or a child with unexplained sweating needs in-person assessment.
Call Back If: persistent or worsening sweating; night sweats, fever, weight loss, palpitations, or functional impact.
